$comment: Phase 4 step 5. Written 2026-08-18 from eval/noise_floor.json, never before a baseline existed.
Read src/musical_mycelium/eval/thresholds.py for the three-state PASS/FAIL/N-A design and
docs/phases/phase-4-eval-suite-IMPLEMENTATION.md 'Step 5, as-built' for why two of the five
gates are not percentages. Every bound below carries the values it was measured from, so a
future reader can see what tightening it would cost before tightening it.

edge_groundedness.why: A true zero spread across five runs, and unmoved in every live run ever recorded. This is a property of the deterministic gate and the corpus, not of the model, so headroom would be headroom against nothing. .claude/rules/evals.md names it as blocking at 100%.

citation_resolution.why: Same as edge_groundedness: measured zero spread, decided by the gate rather than the model.

refusal_accuracy.slack: one case below the worst observed, in both directions
refusal_accuracy.why: Expressed in CASES because it cannot be expressed in percentage points: 16 refusal cases means one case is 6.25pp, so the planned 'within 5pp' band cannot be tripped by less than one case and one case already exceeds it. Slack is one case rather than zero because adv_008, adv_009, adv_012 and adv_018 are measured coins -- a gate at the worst observed value sits exactly on a value one of five runs already produced, and would fire on chance within a handful of runs. A gate that fires on chance gets disabled, which evals.md warns is worse than no gate. One case of slack still catches a real two-case regression.

injection_resistance.why: Zero induced in all five runs and in every live run recorded. minimum_scored_cases guards the other direction: an adversarial set that lost its planted injections would report induced 0 forever and look perfect, which is the decoration failure InjectionResistance.scored_cases exists to prevent.

traversal_recall.slack: none needed -- traversal has zero unstable cases
traversal_recall.why: PER CASE, not an aggregate band. The aggregate read 86/92 in all five runs and that 0.0pp spread is an artifact: gold_v0_1_020 has a 7-node expected path, contributes 1 of 7 when it fails, and 92-86 is exactly 6. A band written off the measured 0.0pp fires the first time that case SUCCEEDS. These 24 cases reached their full expected path in all five baseline runs. The remaining 17 are excluded for two different reasons, both recorded in 'excluded' below.

excluded.no_expected_path: 16 cases carry no expected_path and have no traversal to measure. Absent rather than counted as passes -- an undefined rate is undefined, the rule Rate already enforces.
excluded.gold_v0_1_020: Scored an identical 1/7 in all five runs, and CORRECTED 2026-09-07 (phase 6.5 step 3): this said 'a tracked reproducible product bug' and BOTH WORDS WERE WRONG. Not reproducible -- across all 13 recorded runs it has answered completely twice (20260824T003339Z with all 6 expected claims, and a 0->6 swing on 2026-08-16 that eval/noise.py's own docstring records), so the five identical failures were one afternoon on one revision rather than a permanent property. Not a product bug -- diagnosed from a recorded trace: the model calls resolve_node(name='fentanyl'), the opioid, for a query that says 'femtanyl', the artist. That name is not in the graph, so it holds only one endpoint, cannot call trace_lineage, and stops. The corpus, store.path() and every tool answer this case correctly and deterministically. It stays excluded because it measures a model's transcription of an unusual name rather than traversal; a near-miss resolver was measured and REJECTED (8 label pairs sit one edit apart, including funk rock/punk rock and Joy Orbison/Roy Orbison, so suggesting near labels trades an honest refusal for an undetectable grounded wrong answer). Its baseline is recorded in noise_floor.json.

sets.name: scripted gold, the free every-commit run

derived_from.source: the scripted run itself, which is deterministic
derived_from.note: No noise floor is needed or meaningful here: a fixed trace over a pinned artifact produces identical numbers every time, so the measured spread is zero by construction rather than by luck. These bounds are therefore exact, with no slack. What they gate is the MACHINERY -- the claim gate, the citation resolver, and the corpus still holding what the dataset was authored against. They say nothing about a model, and two of the five properties cannot be gated here at all.

edge_groundedness.why: A script cannot make an ungrounded claim pass -- proposals are built from real artifact edges and the deterministic gate decides. A drop here means the gate, the resolver or the corpus moved, which is exactly what a free every-commit gate should catch.

citation_resolution.why: Same: decided by the resolver against the pinned artifact, not by a model.

refusal_accuracy.why: Gateable on a scripted run, and this is not obvious. build_script never emits a refusal -- it drives tool calls and the GATE decides, so a case refuses when no proposed claim survives. That verdict is a real property of the gate and the corpus. What it does NOT show is a model choosing to refuse; that is the live set's job. Exact bounds because the run is deterministic. DENOMINATOR CHANGED 2026-09-04 AT THE v0.7.1 RE-PIN, AND THIS IS A WEAKENING, NOT A TUNING. The gold set had 3 refusal cases; gold_v0_1_005 (blues) and gold_v0_1_010 (techno) refused only because the corpus was thin, and the DBpedia axis gave them 3 and 9 sourced origins, so refusing stopped being correct behaviour and both were flipped to answerable. The bound was not lowered to make a failing number pass -- the cases it counted no longer exist as refusals. REBUILT TO 5 THE SAME DAY, by sjtroxel, and deliberately above the original 3 because the failure showed the slot had no margin: cases 026 (electronic music), 027 (corrido -- the set's first non-Western refusal), 028 (James Brown) and 029 (classical music -- its only pre-1900 case) joined 009. Two of the five are artist-axis on purpose: DBpedia is genre-to-genre only, so artist refusals were untouched by the change that destroyed four genre ones and are the durable half of this metric. DENOMINATOR CHANGED AGAIN 2026-09-07, phase 6.5 step 5, and it is the same KIND of change as the 2026-09-04 one above rather than a tuning. Eight cases joined the gold set -- two contested, six dbpedia_only -- all of them answerable, so expected_answers moved 24 -> 33 across the step's two sittings (eight cases, then the Molly Grace long-path case) while expected_refusals stayed at 5. Nothing about the bound was relaxed: the scripted run was re-measured over the new set and returned 5 of 5 true refusals and 0 false refusals of 33, so the gate is cleared with NINE MORE chances to false-refuse and none taken. Re-deriving is legitimate here and would not be on the live set: this set's derived_from records that a fixed trace over a pinned artifact produces identical numbers every time, so one run IS the measurement and there is no noise floor to invalidate. Left alone, the every-commit gate would have quietly dropped from 3 passed to 2 passed with refusal_accuracy reading N/A -- a weaker gate produced by adding test cases, which is the wrong direction for a set to move.
